text:
alex.sre: Heads up — after the 03:00 GPU node pool scale-up, controller-manager CPU shot to 95% across control-plane nodes and we started seeing apiserver 5xxs + leader election churn. Anyone digging in?

maria.platform: saw that. node-controller logs show lots of retries binding pods to GPU taints. kubelet logs show plugin restarts (nvidia-device-plugin).

jake.ops: I pulled controller-manager metrics: leader_election_acquired toggling every ~30s, and controller_sync_duration_seconds spiking for node-controller and job-controller.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0318-003 (severity: S2) — paging oncall.

lina-ml: impacted: a couple of Dedicated clusters doing heavy model rollouts — provisioning pods stuck Pending with image pull backoffs and then node not ready. Could be imagepull + device plugin race.

alex.sre: paste of controller-manager logs snippet: 
```
I0318 03:05:02.123456 1 leaderelection.go:243] attempting to acquire leader lease redwood/control-plane-lock
E0318 03:05:32.654321 1 managers.go:201] failed to sync node controller: operation timed out
E0318 03:05:33.000000 1 leaderelection.go:292] failed to update lease: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: error while dialing"
```

maria.platform: apiserver logs show lots of connection reset by peer to etcd around same window. etcd metrics: request_latency_seconds p95 jumped, leader observations show re-election started at 03:05:31.

jake.ops: checking underlying infra — noisy neighbor on storage in us-west-2a? saw elevated iops from etcd snapshots + concurrent node image pulls. Might be hitting cloud disk throughput.

alex.sre: think the sequence is: GPU scale-up triggers many large image pulls (containers with GPU libs), nvidia plugin restarts, kubelets regressing -> node heartbeats fluctuate -> controller-manager tries to reassign pods / mark nodes NotReady -> leader election churn + apiserver overload -> etcd request latency skyrockets -> further control plane failures.

lina-ml: we did push a new container image yesterday with larger layers (~2.3GB). Could explain prolonged pulls.

jake.ops: mitigation idea: 1) pause autoscaling to stop more node churn, 2) throttle image pulls with a staging rollout, 3) increase etcd IO throughput (temporary bigger disk), 4) bump controller-manager leader election lease duration to reduce flapping while investigating. Thoughts?

maria.platform: +1 for pausing autoscaler now. I'll cordon new nodes with GPUs and scale down non-critical nodepools. Also will open cloud support ticket for disk IOPS in us-west-2a.

oncall-bot: @oncall-john paged (paged 1).

alex.sre: logging the quick mitigation: paused cluster-autoscaler on affected clusters, cordoned newly created GPU nodes, bumped etcd snapshot schedule to avoid peak window.

jake.ops: applied a temporary leader-election config override in kustomize to increase leaseDuration to 60s, renewDeadline to 45s (was 15/10s). Pushed rollout to controller-manager replicas 2->3 to reduce failover impact.

lina-ml: for longer term: recommend pre-pulling heavy images on node boot image (image prefetch) and using smaller base images / multi-stage to shrink layers. Also device plugin should be pinned to restart only on driver updates.

maria.platform: putting follow-ups in GH: https://redwood-internal/infra/issues/987 — include action items: pre-pull job, autoscaler max surge limits, disk resize policy, leader-election default tuning doc.

alex.sre: current status — apiserver 5xxs dropped after cordon & leader-election tuning, controller-manager CPU back to ~35%. Still monitoring etcd p95.

jake.ops: leaving note: if we see re-occurrence during next scheduled rollout (04:00), recommend aborting and using canary nodes.

lina-ml: :thumbsup: will coordinate with ML infra to push smaller image in next release window.

maria.platform: closing incident if stable for 30m.

alex.sre: thanks everyone. saving logs to /var/log/eng-sre/1772501123-controlplane-gpu-scale.json and adding to post-incident doc.
